dispositions.impact: Deployment can report ready and release the runner while capture cannot initialize.

findings.title: Portal projects package rows without verifying the immutable evidence chain

evidence.detail: loadCompletedRun validates run IDs, authority flags and verification.outcome, then reads NDJSON directly; it does not verify manifest self-hash, artifact SHA-256, sizes or artifact-sha256.txt.
latestV2Package applies metadata predicates and directly loads normalized rows without cryptographic verification.
The contract describes a projection of durable immutable runs, so omission of digest verification breaks the stated trust boundary.

findings.impact: A corrupted or substituted normalized row can be returned as accepted/healthy by the BFF while the immutable package verifier would reject it. Portal status and UI therefore do not preserve evidence integrity end to end.
findings.recommendation: Before projecting any completed package, execute a read-only verifier that checks manifest self-hash, every declared artifact SHA-256 and size, checksum index, run/request/binding identities, authority flags and row-count geometry. Fail closed to UNAVAILABLE.

findings.title: OKX supplement verifier follows intermediate-directory symlinks outside the package root

evidence.detail: verify_supplement rejects unsafe relative components and a symlink at the final path, but does not inspect intermediate components or prove resolved containment before hashing.
_safe_member shows the stronger required pattern: inspect every component, resolve strictly and require containment.
Focused v2 tests cover normalization, staleness, confirmed candles and exact coverage, but no intermediate-directory symlink case.

findings.impact: A package can reference regular files through a symlinked parent such as candles/okx-swap and pass SHA/size checks against files outside the immutable supplement root. This violates path confinement and allows package substitution.
findings.recommendation: Use one shared safe-member routine for every verifier and add regression tests for symlinked root, parent directory, final file and traversal to both in-root and out-of-root targets.

findings.title: Market Evidence API authorization accepts any production session-cookie value

evidence.detail: All API routes call requireSessionPresence, then continue when a session cookie exists.
Outside fixture mode, requireBrowserSession only checks that __Host-portal_session exists; it does not validate signature, expiry, revocation, tenant membership or role.
The Market Evidence route performs no independent session, tenant or RBAC validation.
Identity and cross-tenant tests execute only in fixture identity mode, which injects explicit states and does not exercise production cookie validation.

findings.impact: A direct client can supply an arbitrary cookie value and cross the application-level authentication gate for read-only Market Evidence APIs. The current data is public-market evidence, but the documented tenant/RBAC boundary is not enforced by the application.
findings.recommendation: Validate the opaque session against the control-plane/session store on every protected request or use a locally verifiable signed/encrypted session with expiry, revocation version, tenant and role checks. Add production-mode forged-cookie and cross-tenant tests.

findings.title: Collectors and deployment checks report healthy when the immutable request is unavailable

evidence.detail: Missing request returns status=blocked, while healthy is true for every status except rejected or failed.
v2 repeats the same blocked-to-healthy derivation.
Healthchecks validate only healthy=true and freshness.
Deployment probes accept any result status not equal to failed or rejected, so blocked is accepted.

findings.impact: A missing, mis-mounted or unreadable request can produce a healthy container and a successful deployment gate while no capture can start. This is false readiness and can conceal the actual operational blocker.
findings.recommendation: Separate liveness from readiness. Require an explicit allowed state set tied to the deployment phase, and reject blocked/CAPTURE_REQUEST_UNAVAILABLE during initialization probes and Docker readiness.

findings.title: Completed-candle availability is backdated to close time without enforcing observed availability in WH-01

evidence.detail: Historical candle pages are fetched during finalization and normalized with available_at_ms equal to close_time_ms_exclusive.
v2 records fetched_at_ms but still sets available_at_ms to candle close.
WH-01 selects candles only by close_time_ms_exclusive and assigns candle-derived metrics available_at_ms=decision_ms; it does not require row.available_at_ms or fetched_at_ms <= decision_ms.

findings.impact: The package proves that exchange history was fetched after the interval, but the materialized model treats each candle as decision-time available. This does not prove point-in-time observability and permits restated/post-hoc data to be represented as prospective evidence.
findings.recommendation: Define observed availability explicitly. Preserve fetched/received time, refuse any row not actually observed by the decision cutoff for prospective use, or label the dataset historical-only and prevent it from satisfying prospective WH-01 readiness.

findings.title: Crash recovery is fail-closed but not restart-resumable at sample and finalization boundaries

evidence.detail: An existing sample-attempt marker becomes a failed sample; an interrupted finalization marker causes terminal rejection rather than deterministic resume.
Partial enrichment with only one of the expected files present cannot be repaired because writes are no-overwrite.
An existing sample root causes failure; there is no staged sample commit or recovery verifier.

findings.impact: SIGKILL, host restart or storage interruption at a narrow write boundary can permanently reject an otherwise valid prospective run, reducing availability and requiring a new immutable request window.
findings.recommendation: Use per-sample staging directories plus atomic rename, verify-and-resume completed stages, and make finalization idempotently resumable without weakening no-overwrite guarantees.

findings.title: Portal cannot classify an old completed immutable package as STALE

evidence.detail: The stale predicate includes latest.run.state !== completed even though latest is selected only from completed runs, making the predicate always false.
STALE is documented as a first-class status and the stale threshold is configurable.

findings.impact: An arbitrarily old completed package remains BLOCKED, LIVE or DEGRADED and cannot surface age-based staleness, hiding operational data-age risk.
findings.recommendation: Define separate freshness rules for active acquisition and latest immutable evidence, derive STALE from capture/verification time, and add clock-controlled tests for completed packages.

findings.title: v1 inner verifier resolves a path before checking whether the declared member is a symlink

evidence.detail: _verify_file_identity resolves the declared path first and then calls is_symlink on the resolved target, so an in-root symlink is not detected.
The outer package service contains a stronger component-wise safe-child check.

findings.impact: The v1 capture verifier does not enforce its regular-file/no-symlink invariant for links whose resolved target remains inside the run root. Outer publication reduces exposure, but the inner verifier is weaker than declared.
findings.recommendation: Validate each unresolved path component before resolving and share the hardened safe-member implementation across v1/v2 verifiers.

findings.title: Collector runtime base images are not digest-pinned and CI/runtime patch versions can drift

evidence.detail: Both collectors use python:3.13-slim-bookworm without a digest.
CI requests Python 3.13 without a patch pin.
Portal demonstrates the stronger digest-pinned base-image pattern.

findings.impact: A rebuild at the same repository SHA can consume a different Python base and patch level, weakening reproducibility and supply-chain attribution.
findings.recommendation: Pin collector bases by digest, record Python patch/package inventory in image labels or SBOM, and align the focused CI patch version with runtime.
